title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has issued a formal response to the 2020 Committee report “Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards,” outlining its priorities for regulating AI. It stresses the need for transparency, accountability, and public trust in AI systems, and commits to developing clear standards and safeguards to protect citizens while fostering innovation.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is developing rules to oversee how artificial intelligence is used in qualifications to keep exams fair, secure, and trustworthy. They will work with educators, exam bodies and the public to set clear guidelines and monitor AI’s impact on assessment quality.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report evaluates how using copyrighted works in training AI systems affects both the creators’ rights and the broader innovation ecosystem. It offers an impact assessment and recommends practical guidelines to balance the protection of intellectual property with the advancement of artificial intelligence technology.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government has responded to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence, emphasizing that the UK must not become complacent about the rapid growth of AI. It outlines plans to strengthen governance, increase investment, and enforce ethical standards to ensure AI development aligns with national interests and public safety.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document explains the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of the committee that will review how artificial intelligence relates to public standards. It also includes a FAQ section that answers common questions about the review process.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on AI governance, outlining its views on regulation, transparency, and accountability. The submission calls for strong oversight mechanisms and collaboration between industry, academia, and policymakers to ensure responsible AI deployment.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explains how artificial intelligence will change the rules for medical products, focusing on making them safer and easier to bring to market. It follows the guidance of the AI White Paper to help developers, regulators, and companies use AI responsibly in medical products.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI‑driven defence group of its size. It plans to do this by developing advanced AI capabilities, setting strong governance and ethical standards, and ensuring that AI enhances operational readiness and strategic advantage.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will collaborate with the transport sector to leverage AI's benefits while addressing potential risks. It outlines partnership strategies, risk mitigation measures, and opportunities to integrate AI into transportation services.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report examines how copyright-protected works are used in AI system development, focusing on compliance with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It highlights current practices, challenges, and policy recommendations to balance innovation with copyright protection.
